title: Snake Game
description: Build a snake game with snake movement, growth, food placement, collision detection, and score tracking.

steps.title: Create the snake as an array of segments
steps.description: Define the `snake` as an array of segment objects with `x` and `y` coordinates. The snake starts as a single segment at the center of a 10x10 grid. Log the snake.
hints: Segment: { x: 5, y: 5 }
Snake array: [{ x: 5, y: 5 }]
Define GRID_SIZE = 10 (grid is GRID_SIZE x GRID_SIZE)

codeTemplate.python:
GRID_SIZE = 10
snake = [{"x": 5, "y": 5}]

import json
print("Snake:", json.dumps(snake))
print("Length:", len(snake))

verification.successMessage: Snake is initialized with a single segment at the center!
verification.failureMessage: Define a GRID_SIZE constant and a snake array with one segment at the center of the grid.

Create new head: { x: head.x + dx, y: head.y + dy }
Add to front: [newHead, ...snake] and remove last: .pop()

Create new head at the front, keep all existing segments
Log: 'Snake grew! Length: ' + snake.length

Check if the random cell overlaps with any snake segment
If overlap, generate new coordinates (loop until valid)

steps.title: Check for collisions
steps.description: Write a `checkCollision` function that checks if the snake's head hits a wall (out of bounds) or the snake's own body. Return true if collision detected. Log test results.
hints: Get head: snake[0]
Wall collision: head.x < 0 || head.x >= GRID_SIZE || head.y < 0 || head.y >= GRID_SIZE
Self collision: loop through snake.slice(1) and check if any segment matches head coordinates

codeTemplate.python:
GRID_SIZE = 10

def checkCollision(snake):
  

# Test wall collision
snake1 = [{"x": -1, "y": 5}]
print("Wall hit:", checkCollision(snake1))

# Test self collision
snake2 = [{"x": 3, "y": 3}, {"x": 4, "y": 3}, {"x": 4, "y": 4}, {"x": 3, "y": 4}, {"x": 3, "y": 3}]
print("Self hit:", checkCollision(snake2))

# Test no collision
snake3 = [{"x": 5, "y": 5}, {"x": 4, "y": 5}]
print("No hit:", checkCollision(snake3))

verification.test: output.includes('Wall hit: true') && output.includes('Self hit: true') && output.includes('No hit: false')
verification.successMessage: Collision detection works for walls, self, and safe positions!
verification.failureMessage: checkCollision should return true when the head is out of bounds or overlaps any body segment, false otherwise.

steps.title: Track the score
steps.description: Create a `score` variable that increments whenever the snake eats food (moves onto the food position). Log the score after eating food.
hints: Initialize let score = 0
After moveSnake, check if head equals food position
If so: increment score, call growSnake, and placeFood again

verification.successMessage: Score increments when the snake eats food!
verification.failureMessage: When the snake head moves to the food position, score should increment to 1.

steps.title: Render the grid to a string
steps.description: Write a `renderGrid` function that returns a string representation of the grid. Use `S` for snake segments, `F` for food, and `.` for empty cells. Log the rendered grid.
hints: Create a GRID_SIZE x GRID_SIZE grid of '.' characters
Place 'S' at each snake segment position
Place 'F' at the food position (overwrites 'S' if food is on snake)
Join rows with newlines for the final string

verification.successMessage: Grid renders correctly with snake, food, and empty cells!
verification.failureMessage: renderGrid should show 'S' for snake segments, 'F' for food, and '.' for empty cells in a GRID_SIZE x GRID_SIZE layout.
